title: Reasoning Shift: How Context Silently Shortens LLM Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2604.01161v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibiting test-time scaling behavior, such as extended reasoning traces and self-verification, have demonstrated remarkable performance on complex, long-term reasoning tasks. However, the robustness of these reasoning behaviors remains underexplored. To investigate this, we conduct a systematic evaluation of multiple reasoning models across three scenarios: (1) problems augmented with lengthy, irrelevant context; (2) multi-turn conversational settings with independent tasks; and (3) problems presented as a subtask within a complex task. We observe an interesting phenomenon: reasoning models tend to produce much shorter reasoning traces (up to 74%) for the same problem under different context conditions compared to the traces produced when the problem is presented in isolation. translated_title: 推理偏移：上下文如何悄无声息地缩短大语言模型的推理
translated_abstract: 具有测试时扩展行为的大语言模型（LLM），例如延长的推理轨迹和自我验证，在复杂的长期推理任务上展现出卓越的性能。然而，这些推理行为的鲁棒性仍未得到充分探索。为了研究这一问题，我们在三种场景下对多个推理模型进行了系统性评估：（1）附加了冗长无关上下文的问题；（2）包含独立任务的多轮对话设置；（3）作为复杂任务中子任务呈现的问题。我们观察到一个有趣的现象：在不同的上下文条件下，推理模型对同一问题产生的推理轨迹比问题单独呈现时短得多（最多缩短74%）。更细粒度的分析表明，这种压缩与自我验证和不确定性管理的减少相关。
tldr: 本研究系统评估发现，上下文条件的变化（如无关冗长信息、多轮对话、子任务情境）会使推理模型对同一问题悄然产生最多缩短74%的推理轨迹，并伴随自我验证和不确定性管理能力的下降，揭示了LLM推理行为的脆弱性。
en_tdlr: This study systematically reveals that context variations—such as lengthy irrelevant information, multi-turn conversations, or subtask settings—silently cause reasoning models to produce reasoning traces shortened by up to 74% for the same problem, accompanied by reduced self-verification and uncertainty management, exposing the fragility of LLM reasoning behaviors.
